title: Federal housing support can exist while Native housing insecurity remains hard to count and underfunded
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-109173 preliminary observations on federal Native housing and homelessness programs, Tribal and TDHE perspectives, and selected site work
geography: American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian communities; Tribes and Tribal Designated Housing Entities

denominator.unit: GAO preliminary review of federal housing support targeted to Native communities

federal_programs_identified.unit: federal programs that can provide housing support targeted to AI/AN and Native Hawaiian populations

funding_adequacy.value: nearly all Tribes and TDHEs contacted said funding was not sufficient to keep pace with construction, rehabilitation, or maintenance needs
funding_adequacy.unit: reported Tribal and Tribal Designated Housing Entity perspective

doubled_up_housing.value: widespread in the preliminary evidence and may not align with federal homelessness definitions
doubled_up_housing.unit: temporarily staying with friends or family; prevalence and duration not estimated nationally

housing_security.unit: household-level prevalence, duration, safety, privacy, stability, repair, and later stay/move outcome

observations.method: Review of GAO preliminary testimony and related work, including identification of federal programs, interviews with Tribes and Tribal Designated Housing Entities, and selected site observations; preliminary qualitative findings are kept separate from national prevalence estimates.
observations.uncertainty: The testimony is preliminary. The program count does not establish usable coverage, and the reported funding and definition concerns do not measure every Tribe, doubled-up household, application, or housing outcome.
observations.subgroup: American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian communities; Tribes, Tribal organizations, Tribal Designated Housing Entities, and households experiencing sheltered, unsheltered, or doubled-up housing insecurity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Doubling up can be a culturally meaningful and protective form of family support, and a federal definition may be intended to target a specific program purpose; the source does not show that every doubled-up arrangement is unsafe or that definitions alone caused the access gap.

related_sources.claim: Official accessible report edition provides the preliminary observations and source context.

boundary: This record captures a preliminary federal-program landscape, reported funding inadequacy, and a possible mismatch between federal homelessness definitions and doubled-up housing insecurity in Native communities. It does not estimate national prevalence, duration, safety, tribal control, application success, construction completion, or durable housing outcomes.
